MicroSkills.name: Model solution components and boundaries
MicroSkills.definition: Describe the components, interfaces and constraints of a proposed solution.

MicroSkills.name: Compare architecture alternatives
MicroSkills.definition: Compare feasible designs against agreed quality, cost and risk criteria.

MicroSkills.name: Specify integration contracts
MicroSkills.definition: Define and check the information exchange and failure behaviour between systems.

MicroSkills.name: Specify measurable service quality targets
MicroSkills.definition: State testable availability, performance and other agreed quality expectations.

MicroSkills.name: Document and explain architecture decisions
MicroSkills.definition: Record a design decision and explain its consequences to the relevant audience.

MicroSkills.name: Assess architecture change impact
MicroSkills.definition: Identify interfaces and quality constraints affected by a proposed design change.

MicroSkills.name: Implement programs and scripts
MicroSkills.definition: Write and check executable logic for a specified software or automation task.

MicroSkills.name: Manage source changes with version control
MicroSkills.definition: Record and review source changes so a tested version can be identified and recovered.

MicroSkills.name: Translate requirements into verifiable changes
MicroSkills.definition: Connect a stated user or service need to a bounded implementation and explicit checks.

MicroSkills.name: Deploy a controlled software release
MicroSkills.definition: Apply an agreed deployment procedure and verify the released service and rollback path.

MicroSkills.name: create data models
MicroSkills.definition: Represent entities, relationships and constraints in a data model.

MicroSkills.name: develop data processing applications
MicroSkills.definition: Implement programs that transform input data into specified outputs.

MicroSkills.name: implement data warehousing techniques
MicroSkills.definition: Apply warehouse structures and loading techniques to analytical data.

MicroSkills.name: Document source-to-target mappings
MicroSkills.definition: Record how source fields become target fields, including transformation rules.

MicroSkills.name: Verify data quality
MicroSkills.definition: Check records against explicit completeness, accuracy and consistency rules.

MicroSkills.name: Maintain metadata documentation
MicroSkills.definition: Record dataset meaning, ownership and structural metadata.

MicroSkills.name: Monitor pipeline operations
MicroSkills.definition: Observe pipeline runs and investigate operational failures.

MicroSkills.name: Design data integration flows
MicroSkills.definition: Specify how data moves between source and destination systems.

MicroSkills.name: Profile source datasets
MicroSkills.definition: Summarise missing values, duplicates and distributions before ingestion.

MicroSkills.name: Implement data extraction
MicroSkills.definition: Extract source records into a controlled staging area.

MicroSkills.name: Implement transformation rules
MicroSkills.definition: Convert values and enforce business rules during data processing.

MicroSkills.name: Orchestrate retry-safe pipeline tasks
MicroSkills.definition: Order dependent tasks and make retries preserve correct outputs.

MicroSkills.name: Optimise warehouse workloads
MicroSkills.definition: Compare access speed and loading cost before selecting a warehouse optimisation.

MicroSkills.name: Apply secure data handling
MicroSkills.definition: Apply access restrictions and approved handling controls to datasets.

MicroSkills.name: Test data pipelines
MicroSkills.definition: Write checks for transformation logic and end-to-end data flow.

MicroSkills.name: Trace data dependencies
MicroSkills.definition: Identify downstream consumers affected by a dataset change.

MicroSkills.name: design user interface
MicroSkills.definition: Specify user interface structure and interactions for a user task.

MicroSkills.name: Implement accessible user interfaces
MicroSkills.definition: Implement interfaces that support keyboard and assistive technology use.

MicroSkills.name: design application interfaces
MicroSkills.definition: Define interfaces through which application components exchange information.

MicroSkills.name: use query languages
MicroSkills.definition: Retrieve and manipulate data using a query language.

MicroSkills.name: integrate system components
MicroSkills.definition: Connect components and verify their combined behaviour.

MicroSkills.name: debug software
MicroSkills.definition: Locate and correct causes of software defects.

MicroSkills.name: perform software unit testing
MicroSkills.definition: Verify individual units of software with repeatable automated checks.

MicroSkills.name: conduct ICT code review
MicroSkills.definition: Review source changes and give actionable technical feedback.

MicroSkills.name: Implement responsive layouts
MicroSkills.definition: Adapt layout and content to different viewport sizes.

MicroSkills.name: Use semantic HTML
MicroSkills.definition: Choose elements whose meaning matches the content and interaction.

MicroSkills.name: Handle asynchronous web requests
MicroSkills.definition: Handle successful responses, HTTP failures and request cancellation in the interface.

MicroSkills.name: Validate application inputs
MicroSkills.definition: Enforce input constraints and provide usable validation feedback on client and server.

MicroSkills.name: Enforce application authorization
MicroSkills.definition: Check permissions for protected actions and resources.

MicroSkills.name: Use database transactions
MicroSkills.definition: Commit related updates atomically and roll back unsuccessful operations.

MicroSkills.name: Improve existing software structure
MicroSkills.definition: Revise existing implementation while checking that required behaviour is preserved.

MicroSkills.name: Configure continuous integration
MicroSkills.definition: Run build and test steps automatically when code changes.

MicroSkills.name: Define data ownership responsibilities
MicroSkills.definition: Identify the accountable owner and handling responsibilities for a specified dataset.

MicroSkills.name: Document data governance rules
MicroSkills.definition: Record agreed rules for data handling, sharing and quality within a defined scope.

MicroSkills.name: Check data lifecycle compliance
MicroSkills.definition: Check evidence of data handling against agreed lifecycle and governance rules.

MicroSkills.name: Configure and verify network connectivity
MicroSkills.definition: Configure a bounded network connection and check addressing, routing and name resolution.

MicroSkills.name: Provision infrastructure resources
MicroSkills.definition: Prepare compute, storage or network resources against an agreed service specification.

MicroSkills.name: Automate infrastructure procedures
MicroSkills.definition: Implement and verify scripts for repeatable infrastructure tasks.

MicroSkills.name: Maintain configuration records
MicroSkills.definition: Keep infrastructure configuration and change records aligned with the deployed state.

MicroSkills.name: Monitor service health
MicroSkills.definition: Collect and interpret service measurements and alerts against agreed operating limits.

MicroSkills.name: Investigate infrastructure faults
MicroSkills.definition: Use observable service evidence to isolate a fault and verify a controlled remedy.

MicroSkills.name: Verify backup and recovery procedures
MicroSkills.definition: Demonstrate restoration of a bounded service or dataset using an agreed recovery procedure.

MicroSkills.name: Apply infrastructure hardening and updates
MicroSkills.definition: Apply approved secure configuration and updates, then check operation and protection.

MicroSkills.name: plan software testing
MicroSkills.definition: Set test scope, approach, resources and completion conditions.

MicroSkills.name: develop ICT test suite
MicroSkills.definition: Organise test cases into a suite linked to intended behaviours.

MicroSkills.name: execute software tests
MicroSkills.definition: Run specified tests and record observed results.

MicroSkills.name: report test findings
MicroSkills.definition: Communicate test results and defects with supporting evidence.

MicroSkills.name: replicate customer software issues
MicroSkills.definition: Reproduce a reported issue under identified conditions.

MicroSkills.name: develop automated software tests
MicroSkills.definition: Implement repeatable automated tests with meaningful assertions.

MicroSkills.name: execute integration testing
MicroSkills.definition: Test interactions and data exchange between components.

MicroSkills.name: Perform structured exploratory testing
MicroSkills.definition: Investigate software using a defined exploratory testing charter.

MicroSkills.name: Apply equivalence partitioning
MicroSkills.definition: Select representative cases from distinct valid and invalid input classes.

MicroSkills.name: Apply boundary value analysis
MicroSkills.definition: Test values at and around the boundaries of ordered input classes.

MicroSkills.name: Prioritise tests by risk
MicroSkills.definition: Order tests using failure likelihood and product impact.

MicroSkills.name: Prepare test data and environments
MicroSkills.definition: Set up controlled inputs and system conditions required for repeatable tests.

MicroSkills.name: Classify defect impact
MicroSkills.definition: Describe defect severity and propose a repair priority with evidence.

MicroSkills.name: Run regression tests
MicroSkills.definition: Check that changes have not broken previously working behaviour.

MicroSkills.name: Execute performance tests
MicroSkills.definition: Measure response behaviour under a defined workload and environment.

MicroSkills.name: Investigate flaky automated tests
MicroSkills.definition: Use retry results and controlled reruns to diagnose inconsistent test outcomes.

MicroSkills.name: Analyse information security risks
MicroSkills.definition: Identify a bounded security risk, its affected assets and a justified treatment proposal.

MicroSkills.name: Select and verify security controls
MicroSkills.definition: Choose controls for a stated threat or requirement and check their intended protection.

MicroSkills.name: Configure identity and access controls
MicroSkills.definition: Configure and test authentication or authorization rules against an agreed access policy.

MicroSkills.name: Investigate security alerts
MicroSkills.definition: Interpret a security alert and supporting records to decide a justified next action.

MicroSkills.name: Execute a security incident response procedure
MicroSkills.definition: Apply an agreed incident procedure while preserving records and verifying containment.

MicroSkills.name: Assess technical vulnerabilities
MicroSkills.definition: Identify and validate findings in an authorized assessment scope and explain their impact.

MicroSkills.name: Verify vulnerability remediation
MicroSkills.definition: Apply or coordinate an agreed remedy and check that the relevant finding is resolved.

MicroSkills.name: Document security control assurance
MicroSkills.definition: Connect a security requirement, control and check result in a reviewable assurance record.

MicroSkills.name: Communicate security recommendations
MicroSkills.definition: Explain a security finding, decision or control to the audience responsible for action.

MicroSkills.name: Maintain security policy procedures
MicroSkills.definition: Keep an agreed security policy and its operating procedures consistent with the stated scope.

LearningModules.title: Junior Data modelling and storage - Module 1: Guided implementation
LearningModules.learningOutcome:
In Data modelling and storage, demonstrate the following junior tasks:
MS-DE01: Create an entity model from supplied requirements; verify keys and relationships against sample records.
MS-DE03: Build and load a small warehouse using a supplied schema and reconcile source-to-target counts.
MS-DE06: Fill a supplied data dictionary with field meanings, owners and structural metadata.
Submit evidence:
MS-DE01: Model diagram, schema, constraint checks and design rationale.
MS-DE03: Warehouse schema, load scripts, history tests and reconciliation results.
MS-DE06: Data dictionary, ownership records, change history and review findings.

LearningModules.title: Junior Data modelling and storage - Module 2: Guided validation
LearningModules.learningOutcome:
In Data modelling and storage, demonstrate the following junior tasks:
MS-DE13: Measure a supplied warehouse query before and after one guided optimisation; confirm unchanged results.
MS-DE16: Identify downstream consumers of a supplied dataset change using existing lineage information.
Submit evidence:
MS-DE13: Workload definition, before/after measurements, result reconciliation and decision record.
MS-DE16: Dependency map, affected-consumer list, assumptions and change verification results.

rubricDefinitions.score0: Observed submitted result is unusable or contradicts the assigned task. Missing evidence is NOT_ASSESSED.
rubricDefinitions.score1: Major errors prevent the main task from succeeding.
rubricDefinitions.score2: Main path works; material edge cases or constraints remain unresolved.
rubricDefinitions.score3: Agreed main, boundary and failure checks pass; only minor non-blocking issues remain.
rubricDefinitions.score4: All agreed checks pass and additional justified checks support robust correctness.
rubricDefinitions.evidenceRule: Artifact and expected/actual checks tied to the assigned skill task.

rubricDefinitions.score0: Submitted verification is inspectable, but its checks are invalid or do not test the claimed behaviour.
rubricDefinitions.score1: Claims rely on unrepeatable or incomplete demonstrations.
rubricDefinitions.score2: Main-path evidence is repeatable; important failure cases or provenance are missing.
rubricDefinitions.score3: Evidence is reproducible and covers agreed boundary/failure cases with traceable inputs.
rubricDefinitions.score4: Evidence is reproducible, risk-based and includes independent cross-checks plus explicit limitations.
rubricDefinitions.evidenceRule: Inputs, method, outputs, logs and relevant failure/boundary cases.

rubricDefinitions.score0: Cannot perform the task even with the permitted support.
rubricDefinitions.score1: Needs substantial support beyond the level allowance.
rubricDefinitions.score2: Completes most work within the allowance, but needs extra corrective intervention.
rubricDefinitions.score3: Completes the agreed scope within the level allowance and escalates justified uncertainties.
rubricDefinitions.score4: Meets level allowance throughout; anticipates and resolves relevant issues without extra corrective help.
rubricDefinitions.evidenceRule: Record assessor interventions and distinguish permitted guidance from corrective help.

rubricDefinitions.score0: Cannot explain the work or its purpose.
rubricDefinitions.score1: Explanation misses key decisions or contradicts the evidence.
rubricDefinitions.score2: Explains main steps but misses a material assumption, limitation or alternative.
rubricDefinitions.score3: Explains decisions, assumptions and limitations with evidence at the assigned level.
rubricDefinitions.score4: Defends decisions against relevant alternatives and incorporates review feedback with evidence.
rubricDefinitions.evidenceRule: Written or oral rationale linked to artifacts and the assigned level.

rubricDefinitions.score0: An inspectable attempt fails to demonstrate the required foundation.
rubricDefinitions.score1: Major mistakes invalidate the foundation behaviour.
rubricDefinitions.score2: Demonstrates the main behaviour but a material required condition fails.
rubricDefinitions.score3: Demonstrates every required foundation condition on the supplied bounded scenario.
rubricDefinitions.score4: Demonstrates the foundation and handles a relevant counterexample correctly.
rubricDefinitions.evidenceRule: Artifact or demonstration showing the readinessOutcome on the supplied scenario.

rubricDefinitions.score0: Submitted checks are inspectable but invalid.
rubricDefinitions.score1: Checks are mostly assertions without reproducible comparisons.
rubricDefinitions.score2: A valid main-case check is provided but a required counterexample or trace is missing.
rubricDefinitions.score3: Expected and observed results can be reproduced for the main case and counterexample.
rubricDefinitions.score4: Independent checks corroborate the result and explain limitations.
rubricDefinitions.evidenceRule: Inputs, expected and observed results, and repeatable verification steps.

rubricDefinitions.score0: An observed explanation contradicts the demonstrated behaviour.
rubricDefinitions.score2: Explains the main behaviour but misses a relevant assumption.
rubricDefinitions.score3: Explains why the foundation is needed and one limitation.
rubricDefinitions.score4: Explains the dependency, a counterexample and the consequence of a violated assumption.
rubricDefinitions.evidenceRule: A short written or recorded explanation tied to the evidence.
